# Implement block: Sand Hourglass (React Native)

You are adding the "Sand Hourglass" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A focus timer with an hourglass for a clock, standing on a linen-coloured table in afternoon light: a frameless glass between two pale oak caps, its bulbs catching white streaks and the reflection of a window, holding 2,300 grains of terracotta sand, each a tiny lit bead. The glass throws a long, soft shadow across the table to the right, with a warm patch of light where the sun passes through an empty bulb. Below it sit a large timer and a line of text, and at the bottom a ruler of minutes under an orange needle. Slide the ruler to choose from 1 to 60 minutes, then turn the glass over by dragging around it, twisting it with two fingers or tapping it: the sand runs through the neck at the pace that empties the top bulb on time, the timer counts down what is left and says when the session ends, and when the last grain lands a band of light crosses the glass and the timer reads "Well done".

**Motion.** The sand is a grid of 77 × 151 cells of 2.2 pt in the glass's own frame, run 4 passes per tick: each grain moves one cell along gravity, else diagonally (the downhill side first once gravity is more than 0.12 of an eighth of a turn off the grid), else, with a 32% chance, two cells sideways and one down, which lays the pile at about 34°. Gravity is the screen's down seen from the turned glass, snapped to the nearest of 8 grid directions, so the grains slide while it turns. The neck sets the pace: a grain may only enter its middle row with a token, and tokens come at 2,300 ÷ (minutes × 60) per second (at most 2 saved up); fully open, the one-cell neck passes about 219 grains a second. The timer is the share of the grains still above the neck times the session's length. The glass's angle is a spring (stiffness 38, damping 7.4: a half turn in about 0.8 s with a small sway); a drag turns it by the finger's angle around its centre and a two-finger twist by the twist, a release throws it 0.22 s ahead at the finger's spin and the spring lands it on the nearest way up, and a tap sends it over; a medium haptic marks a turn made by hand as it lands. While it lies on its side the glass shrinks by up to 10% as if lifted, and its shadow softens and fades by up to 85%. A session starts as the glass goes over (turned straight back within 2 s, it simply returns to being set) and ends 0.35 s after the last grain leaves the neck with the glass at rest: a success haptic, a band of light crossing the glass in 1.15 s, and "Well done" with the minutes focused for 2.6 s before the ruler returns. Turning the glass mid-session runs the sand back, as a real one does. The ruler moves 11 pt per minute, gives way past 1 and 60, coasts after a flick (at most 60 min/s, decaying at 4.5/s) and below 2 min/s snaps to a whole minute on a spring (220/28), with a selection haptic per minute (at most one every 40 ms); it fades away while a session runs. Labels swap in two halves, the old one fading out before the new one fades in, at a rate of 6/s. The shadow is the glass's silhouette laid on the table: a point h above it falls h × 0.92 to the right and h × 0.2 back, its depth 30% of the glass's width, and the patch of light in it shines at up to 55% as a bulb empties. One fixed 1/60 s tick drives the sand, the spring, the ruler and the script, at most 3 ticks a frame. autoPlay (LOOP = 18 s) pulls the ruler from 25 to 40 minutes (0.6 to 1.5 s) and back to 25 (1.9 to 2.7 s), turns the glass over at 3.1 s with the neck fully open so the sand runs out in about 10.5 s, shows the end of the session and rests; a touch pauses it for 4 s. Under Reduce Motion autoPlay stays off, the glass turns over at once without lifting, a flick of the ruler does not coast and the light sweep stays off; the sand still pours. Each grain is drawn as a lit bead by a small shader that reads the grid as a 77 × 151 image; on Android below 13, which has no runtime shaders, each grain is drawn as its plain coloured cell.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/progress/sand-hourglass/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [SandHourglass.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/progress/sand-hourglass/SandHourglass.tsx)
- [sandHourglassEngine.ts](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/progress/sand-hourglass/sandHourglassEngine.ts)
- [sandHourglassSim.ts](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/progress/sand-hourglass/sandHourglassSim.ts)

### Packages

- `@shopify/react-native-skia`
- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-status-bar`
- `react-native-gesture-handler`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
